# rprime

**rprime** is an R package for parsing `.txt` files generated by
E-Prime, a program for running psychological experiments.

## Overview

The main workflow for rprime involves:

1.  [`read_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/read_eprime.md):
    reliably read in data from an Eprime log (`.txt`) file.
2.  [`FrameList()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/FrameList.md):
    extract the text in each `"LogFrame"` in the file, storing each
    log-frame as an R list.
3.  [`preview_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md),
    [`preview_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md):
    explore the structure of the parsed data.
4.  [`keep_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md),
    [`drop_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md),
    [`filter_in()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md),
    [`filter_out()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md):
    select and filter particular levels from the txt-file.
5.  [`to_data_frame()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/to_data_frame.md):
    make a dataframe from the parsed data.

## Installation

To get the current, released version from CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("rprime")
```

## Examples

### Getting data into R

Use
[`example_eprime_file()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/example_eprime_file.md)
to locate a bundled example file. Call it without arguments to list the
available short names and full filenames.

Load the file with
[`read_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/read_eprime.md)
and parse its contents with
[`FrameList()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/FrameList.md).

``` r

library(rprime)
# Read in an Eprime text file
experiment_lines <- read_eprime(example_eprime_file("SAILS1"))

# Extract and parse the log-frames from the file
experiment_data <- FrameList(experiment_lines)
```

### Exploring

In the text file, frames were distinguished by the procedure they run as
well as their level of nesting. Get an overview of the different types
of frames with
[`preview_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md).

``` r

# There are six different kinds of frames in this file
preview_levels(experiment_data)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level       Running         Procedure freq
#>             1        Header            Header    1
#>             3 PracticeBlock PracticeTrialProc   10
#>             2  PracticeList      PracticeProc    1
#>             3    TrialLists         TrialProc   70
#>             2     BlockList         BlockProc    7
#>             1          <NA>              <NA>    1
```

[`preview_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md),
[`preview_frames()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md),
and
[`preview_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md)
return the input object invisibly while printing their previews. The
returned frames can be assigned to a variable or passed to the next step
in a pipeline.

Get a preview of the data in each kind of frame with
[`preview_frames()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md).

``` r

preview_frames(experiment_data)
#> 
#>  Eprime.Level Running Procedure
#>             1  Header    Header
#> List of 22
#>  $ Eprime.Level       : num 1
#>  $ Eprime.LevelName   : chr "Header_"
#>  $ Eprime.Basename    : chr "SAILS_001X00XS1"

#>  $ Procedure          : chr "Header"
#>  $ Running            : chr "Header"
#>  $ VersionPersist     : chr "1"
#>  $ LevelName          : chr "LogLevel10"

#>  $ SessionTime        : chr "11:00:00"
#>  $ SessionTimeUtc     : chr "5:00:00 PM"

#>  $ Age                : chr "00"
#>  $ Gender             : chr "X"
#>  $ Session            : chr "1"
```

[`preview_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md)
prints both kinds of previews (levels and frames).

### Filtering

Use
[`keep_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md)
and
[`drop_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md)
to filter frames according to nesting level.

``` r

# Filter (out) by depth of nesting
not_level_1 <- drop_levels(experiment_data, 1)
preview_levels(not_level_1)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level       Running         Procedure freq
#>             3 PracticeBlock PracticeTrialProc   10
#>             2  PracticeList      PracticeProc    1
#>             3    TrialLists         TrialProc   70
#>             2     BlockList         BlockProc    7

# Filter (in) by depth of nesting
just_level_3 <- keep_levels(experiment_data, 3)
preview_levels(just_level_3)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level       Running         Procedure freq
#>             3 PracticeBlock PracticeTrialProc   10
#>             3    TrialLists         TrialProc   70
```

Use
[`filter_in()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md)
and
[`filter_out()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md)
to filter frames using attribute values. Use repeated filtering
statements to drill down into the list of frames.

``` r

# Filter (out) by attribute values
no_header <- filter_out(experiment_data, "Running", values = "Header")
preview_levels(no_header)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level       Running         Procedure freq
#>             3 PracticeBlock PracticeTrialProc   10
#>             2  PracticeList      PracticeProc    1
#>             3    TrialLists         TrialProc   70
#>             2     BlockList         BlockProc    7
#>             1          <NA>              <NA>    1

# Filter (in) by attribute values
not_practice <- filter_in(experiment_data, "Running", "TrialLists")
preview_levels(not_practice)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level    Running Procedure freq
#>             3 TrialLists TrialProc   70

# Drill down further into the trials by filtering again
sue_trials <- filter_in(not_practice, "Module", "SUE")
preview_eprime(sue_trials)
#> Level Counts: 
#>  Eprime.Level    Running Procedure freq
#>             3 TrialLists TrialProc   30
#> 
#>  Eprime.Level    Running Procedure
#>             3 TrialLists TrialProc
#> List of 25
#>  $ Eprime.Level            : num 3
#>  $ Eprime.LevelName        : chr "TrialLists_5"
#>  $ Eprime.Basename         : chr "SAILS_001X00XS1"
#>  $ Eprime.FrameNumber      : chr "57"
#>  $ Procedure               : chr "TrialProc"
#>  $ Running                 : chr "TrialLists"
#>  $ Sound                   : chr "SUE4.WAV"
#>  $ Correct                 : chr "Word"
#>  $ SueLevel1               : chr "10"
#>  $ Module                  : chr "SUE"
#>  $ Color                   : chr "blue"
#>  $ WordImage               : chr "sue"
#>  $ NonWordImage            : chr "notsue"
#>  $ PuzzleImage             : chr "madagascar"
#>  $ TrialSlide.OnsetDelay   : chr "127"
#>  $ TrialSlide.OnsetTime    : chr "1360767"
#>  $ TrialSlide.DurationError: chr "-999999"
#>  $ TrialSlide.RTTime       : chr "0"
#>  $ TrialSlide.ACC          : chr "0"
#>  $ TrialSlide.RT           : chr "0"
#>  $ TrialSlide.RESP         : chr ""
#>  $ TrialSlide.CRESP        : chr ""
#>  $ Response                : chr "Word"
#>  $ Cycle                   : chr "1"
#>  $ Sample                  : chr "41"
#>  - attr(*, "class")= chr [1:2] "EprimeFrame" "list"
```

### Exporting

Convert to a dataframe with
[`to_data_frame()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/to_data_frame.md).
Attribute names in the log-frames become column names in the dataframe.

``` r

# Export to dataframe
sue_trials_df <- to_data_frame(sue_trials)
str(sue_trials_df)
#> 'data.frame':    30 obs. of  27 variables:
#>  $ Eprime.Level            : num  3 3 3 3 3 ...
#>  $ Eprime.LevelName        : chr  "TrialLists_5" "TrialLists_5" ...
#>  $ Eprime.Basename         : chr  "SAILS_001X00XS1" "SAILS_001X00XS1" ...
#>  $ Eprime.FrameNumber      : chr  "57" "58" ...
#>  $ Procedure               : chr  "TrialProc" "TrialProc" ...
#>  $ Running                 : chr  "TrialLists" "TrialLists" ...
#>  $ Sound                   : chr  "SUE4.WAV" "SUE15.WAV" ...
#>  $ Correct                 : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...
#>  $ SueLevel1               : chr  "10" "2" ...
#>  $ Module                  : chr  "SUE" "SUE" ...
#>  $ Color                   : chr  "blue" "blue" ...
#>  $ WordImage               : chr  "sue" "sue" ...
#>  $ NonWordImage            : chr  "notsue" "notsue" ...
#>  $ PuzzleImage             : chr  "madagascar" "madagascar" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.OnsetDelay   : chr  "127" "98" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.OnsetTime    : chr  "1360767" "1364450" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.DurationError: chr  "-999999" "-999999" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.RTTime       : chr  "0" "0" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.ACC          : chr  "0" "0" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.RT           : chr  "0" "0" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.RESP         : chr  "" "" ...
#>  $ TrialSlide.CRESP        : chr  "" "" ...
#>  $ Response                : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...
#>  $ Cycle                   : chr  "1" "1" ...
#>  $ Sample                  : chr  "41" "42" ...
#>  $ SueLevel2               : chr  NA NA ...
#>  $ SueLevel3               : chr  NA NA ...

# Don't need every column
columns_to_keep <- c(
  "Eprime.Basename", "Module", "Sample", "Correct", "Response"
)
sue_trials_df <- sue_trials_df[columns_to_keep]
head(sue_trials_df)
#>   Eprime.Basename Module Sample Correct Response
#> 1 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     41    Word     Word
#> 2 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     42 NotWord  NotWord
#> 3 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     43 NotWord     Word
#> 4 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     44    Word     Word
#> 5 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     45 NotWord  NotWord
#> 6 SAILS_001X00XS1    SUE     46    Word     Word
```

**Note**: Values read from the text file remain character values in the
final dataframe. You can use
[`readr::type_convert()`](https://readr.tidyverse.org/reference/type_convert.html)
to correct the column types:

``` r

# Right now the sample numbers are stored as character values
str(sue_trials_df)
#> 'data.frame':    30 obs. of  5 variables:
#>  $ Eprime.Basename: chr  "SAILS_001X00XS1" "SAILS_001X00XS1" ...
#>  $ Module         : chr  "SUE" "SUE" ...
#>  $ Sample         : chr  "41" "42" ...
#>  $ Correct        : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...
#>  $ Response       : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...

library(readr)
sue_trials_df <- type_convert(sue_trials_df)
#> 
#> ── Column specification ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> cols(
#>   Eprime.Basename = col_character(),
#>   Module = col_character(),
#>   Sample = col_double(),
#>   Correct = col_character(),
#>   Response = col_character()
#> )
# Now, they are stored as integers...
str(sue_trials_df)
#> 'data.frame':    30 obs. of  5 variables:
#>  $ Eprime.Basename: chr  "SAILS_001X00XS1" "SAILS_001X00XS1" ...
#>  $ Module         : chr  "SUE" "SUE" ...
#>  $ Sample         : num  41 42 43 44 45 ...
#>  $ Correct        : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...
#>  $ Response       : chr  "Word" "NotWord" ...
```

# Package index

## Most important functions

- [`read_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/read_eprime.md)
  : Read in a text file generated by Eprime

- [`example_eprime_file()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/example_eprime_file.md)
  : Locate a bundled example Eprime file

- [`FrameList()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/FrameList.md)
  :

  Convert lines from an Eprime file into `EprimeFrame` objects

- [`filter_in()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md)
  [`filter_out()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/filter_in.md)
  :

  Filter levels in or out of a `FrameList` based on attribute values

- [`keep_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md)
  [`drop_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/keep_levels.md)
  :

  Filter levels in or out of a `FrameList` based on `Eprime.Level`
  values

- [`to_data_frame()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/to_data_frame.md)
  :

  Convert `EprimeFrame` objects into dataframes

## Supporting functions

These help with the parsing of the text file.

- [`listify()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/listify.md) :
  Convert a vector of colon-separated text lines into a list of named
  elements
- [`extract_chunks()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/extract_chunks.md)
  : Extract log-frames from an Eprime log file
- [`preview_eprime()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md)
  [`preview_levels()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md)
  [`preview_frames()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/preview_eprime.md)
  : Preview the levels in a parsed Eprime file

## Objects

These objects represent chunks of data.

- [`EprimeFrame()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/EprimeFrame.md)
  :

  Create an `EprimeFrame` object

- [`as.EprimeFrame()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/as.EprimeFrame.md)
  :

  Convert a list into an `EprimeFrame` object

- [`as.FrameList()`](https://www.tjmahr.com/rprime/reference/as.FrameList.md)
  :

  Convert a list of `EprimeFrame` objects into a `FrameList` object
